questions.question:
Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following sets.

(Note: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding/subtracting/multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)

(18, 162, 9)

(21, 189, 9)
questions.solution:
The logic followed here is:

**Logic: **(a, b, c) → a × c = b

18 × 9 = 162

21 × 9 = 189

Let's check each option:

 
• 
 
(15, 135, 9) → 15 × 9 = 135

 
 
• 
 
(9, 90, 9) → 9 × 9 = 81 ≠ 90

 
 
• 
 
(16, 144, 8) → 16 × 8 = 128 ≠ 144

 
 
• 
 
(12, 120, 9) → 12 × 9 = 108 ≠ 120

 

Thus, (15, 135, 9) is the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as the given sets.

Hence, the correct answer is "**Option 1**".

Read the given statement(s) and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statement(s).

**Statements**:

All cups are glasses.

All glasses are tiles.

**Conclusions: **

(I) Some tiles are glasses.

(II) All cups are tiles159.0
questions.solution:
**Statements:**

Some Robins are Penguins.

All Penguins are Magpies.

All Magpies are Eagles.

The least possible Venn diagram for the given statement is:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a5f237f4042edd3f5bd792d43ada963efc57cd653dc3715767610023a03cc2a4.png] 

**Conclusions:**

(I) All Penguins are Eagles. - Follow (Because, all Penguins are Magpies and all Magpies are Eagles, which means all Penguins are Eagles.)

(II) Some Magpies are Robins. - Follow (Because, some Robins are Penguins and all Penguins are Magpies, which means some Magpies are Robins.)

Thus, both conclusions (I) and (II) follow.

Hence, the correct answer is "**Option 1**".

questions.question:
What should come in place of the question mark (?) in the given series?

612 610 606 600 592 ?3902
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Identify the difference between consecutive terms:

612 − 2 = 610

610 − 4 = 606

606 − 6 = 600

600 − 8 = 592

The next difference is −10: 592 − 10 = 582

**∴ The correct answer is 582.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given series: 612, 610, 606, 600, 592, ?

 612
 
 −2
 →
 
 610
 
 −4
 →
 
 606
 
 −6
 →
 
 600
 
 −8
 →
 
 592
 
 −10
 →
 
 582

The pattern follows the subtraction of consecutive even numbers: 2, 4, 6, 8, 10.

⇒ 612 − 2 = 610

⇒ 610 − 4 = 606

⇒ 606 − 6 = 600

⇒ 600 − 8 = 592

⇒ 592 − 10 = 582

**∴ The correct answer is 582.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Arithmetic Difference Series

A series where the difference between consecutive terms forms another simple sequence like even numbers, odd numbers, or prime numbers.

Decreasing Number Series

In a decreasing series, the value of the terms decreases over time. The logic is typically based on subtraction or division.

Double Difference Method

If the first layer of differences does not show a clear pattern, check the difference between the differences (second layer) to find a constant value or arithmetic progression.</p
